candidate_binding.basis: SHA256 of the exact input_manifest string, identical in all three effect receipts
candidate_binding.manifest_vs_disk: 10/10 recomputed by me from current bytes, drift 0

findings.detail: input_manifest is byte-identical across activate-build-1, activate-test-1 and activate-smoke-write-1: same 1420-character string, same SHA256 f217359b368f8a0714503bc7a87b001ee1e41d51919608382ec0bfd5e580da65. Each receipt's declared input_sha256 equals my recomputation.

The manifest's 10 entries were each recomputed by me from current disk bytes: 10/10 match, drift 0. Coverage is exactly the 4 harness sources (admission, operations, successor_mcp, development) and the 6 named test modules.
activate-build-1 output is 7911 bytes and its declared output_sha256 equals my recomputation over those bytes.
activate-smoke-write-1 output is 64 bytes and its declared output_sha256 equals my recomputation.

activate-test-1 output is stored at EXACTLY 8192 bytes and its declared output_sha256 910c48f99747567f1e229ef5c430ab9bb707440d6dabd10c1ca5053b39bd5a30 does NOT equal my recomputation 0ad542ecab6cd78de29bca327b4c087b98dba7837f9cbd5572296311957f478e over the stored bytes. The stored output begins mid-word with "est...ok", so it is head-truncated and the tail was retained. The declared digest therefore attests an untruncated output I do not possess. This is not evidence of tampering; it is an absence of verifiable integrity for the one artifact that carries the central 83/83 claim. Because the digest cannot match the retained bytes either way, a mismatch here is uninformative and the digest provides no integrity guarantee for what I can read.

All six named modules occur in the retained output, searched as substrings rather than line-start, as instructed: harness_successor_test x1 (at the truncated head, consistent with interleaved diagnostics), harness_development_test x16, harness_authority_test x18, harness_sa_plan_boundary_test x6, mcp_authz_wiring_test x18, mcp_catalog_truth_test x6.
The retained tail contains 'All 83 tests passed.' and 'successor verification: ok'. Reported count parsed as 83. These are read from bytes whose integrity I could not verify; see A-TEST-DIGEST.

Scanned the test output for sendMessage, api.telegram.org, production and admitted tokens. The only hit is one occurrence of 'production' inside the TEST NAME harness_development_test: production_wrong_worker_attempt_and_expiry_are_rejected_test, which is a rejection test and not an effect. The smoke artifact declares scope local_development_only, production_admission false, telegram_traffic false.

The only observed write artifact is governance/planning/20261027-0532-hive-mcp-smoke.json, which is inside the three declared write paths of the approved grant. No write outside the declared set was observed in these receipts.

hold_reason: A-TEST-DIGEST. Every other check passes and the candidate binding is strong, but the single artifact carrying the activation's central claim (83/83 tests passed) has no verifiable integrity against the bytes available to me.
missing_evidence_required_to_clear: M-1 Supply the UNTRUNCATED activate-test-1 output whose SHA256 equals the declared 910c48f997..., or

M-2 Supply an additional digest computed over the RETAINED 8192 bytes together with an explicit truncation declaration (for example retained_bytes, truncation: head, full_output_sha256), so that what a reviewer can read is itself integrity-checked, or
M-3 Supply a per-module pass/count receipt for the six named modules, which would make the 83 total verifiable by parts rather than by an unverifiable whole.
